skill.name: biopython
skill.description: Use Biopython for Python-based molecular biology workflows, including sequence I/O, NCBI Entrez access, BLAST parsing, structural bioinformatics, phylogenetics, and motif analysis.
skill.summary: Guides Biopython workflows for sequences, NCBI databases, BLAST, structures, phylogenetics, and molecular biology analysis.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static alerts were reviewed in context. They are documentation examples or Markdown syntax, including local file examples, public links, placeholder API key text, and code fences. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious execution intent was found.

remediation.issue: Placeholder API key examples may be copied into real projects.
remediation.suggestion: Show environment-variable loading and warn users not to commit real NCBI API keys.

remediation.issue: Markdown code fences caused many command-execution false positives.
remediation.suggestion: Keep shell examples clearly labeled as documentation and avoid ambiguous backtick formatting.

remediation.issue: Network examples depend on user-requested NCBI and BLAST access.
remediation.suggestion: State that online database calls require network access and must respect NCBI rate limits.

content.user_title: Build Biopython Workflows for Molecular Biology
content.value_statement: Bioinformatics tasks often require precise sequence, database, BLAST, and structure code. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Biopython workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides sequence parsing, conversion, translation, transcription, and reverse-complement tasks with Bio.Seq and Bio.SeqIO.
Shows NCBI Entrez search, fetch, PubMed, GenBank, Protein, and Gene workflows with rate-limit notes.
Documents online and local BLAST searches, XML parsing, tabular parsing, and result filtering.
Explains PDB structure parsing, residue access, atom access, DSSP use, superposition, and ligand-contact analysis.
Provides phylogenetic tree reading, construction, manipulation, visualization, and distance examples.
Includes motif, population genetics, restriction analysis, clustering, and sequence utility patterns.
limitations: Requires Python, NumPy, and an installed Biopython environment for execution.
NCBI and BLAST examples can depend on external network access and rate limits.
Does not include a runnable package, tests, or automated pipeline scripts.
Some structure workflows require local tools such as DSSP or local BLAST databases.

use_cases.title: Convert Sequence Files
use_cases.description: Convert FASTA, GenBank, and FASTQ files while preserving IDs, descriptions, and annotations.

use_cases.title: Retrieve NCBI Records
use_cases.description: Search PubMed or GenBank, fetch records, and plan rate-limited database workflows.

use_cases.title: Inspect Protein Structures
use_cases.description: Parse PDB files, navigate chains and residues, and summarize structural measurements.

prompt_templates.title: Parse Sequence Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Biopython skill to read a FASTA file, report sequence IDs and lengths, and explain each step.

prompt_templates.title: Search NCBI Entrez
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Biopython skill to search PubMed for a topic, fetch top records, and summarize rate-limit considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze BLAST Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Biopython skill to parse BLAST XML, filter hits by e-value and identity, and describe the strongest matches.

prompt_templates.title: Build Integrated Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Biopython skill to design a workflow that fetches sequences, aligns them, builds a tree, and records parameters.

output_examples.input: Summarize how to parse a FASTA file and filter long sequences.
output_examples.output: A concise workflow that reads records with Bio.SeqIO, filters by length, and recommends iterator-based processing for large files.

output_examples.input: Plan a PubMed search for papers about a gene family.
output_examples.output: A database workflow covering Entrez email setup, query design, result fetching, rate limits, and record summaries.

output_examples.input: Explain how to compare two protein structures.
output_examples.output: A structural workflow covering PDB parsing, chain selection, atom matching, superposition, RMSD calculation, and validation checks.

best_practices: Set Entrez.email and document API use before calling NCBI services.
Use iterators and small test files before processing large sequence datasets.
Validate file formats, record IDs, and biological assumptions before interpreting results.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real API keys into shared prompts or committed examples.
Do not run large BLAST jobs against NCBI without checking rate limits and batching guidance.
Do not assume every sequence, record, or structure file has complete annotations.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It guides Biopython tasks for sequences, databases, BLAST, structures, phylogenetics, and advanced molecular biology workflows.

faq.question: Does it run analysis automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides reference guidance and code patterns. You still need a Python environment with Biopython installed.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Only for NCBI Entrez, online BLAST, and documentation links. Local file parsing and many analyses work offline.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How should I handle API keys?
faq.answer: Use environment variables or a secure secret store. Do not commit real NCBI API keys.

faq.question: What files are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers FASTA, GenBank, FASTQ, PDB, mmCIF, Newick, NEXUS, phyloXML, and related formats.
